quotes.text: The highest excellence is like that of water. The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things, and in its occupying, without striving to the contrary, the low place which all men dislike.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: Who can make the muddy water clear? Let it be still, and it will gradually become clear. Who can secure the condition of rest? Let movement go on, and the condition of rest will gradually arise.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: The state of vacancy should be brought to the utmost degree, and that of stillness guarded with unwearying vigour. All things alike go through their processes of activity, and then we see them return to their original state.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: This returning to their root is what we call the state of stillness; and that stillness may be called a reporting that they have fulfilled their appointed end.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent. He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: He who is satisfied with his lot is rich; he who goes on acting with energy has a firm will.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: The soft overcomes the hard; and the weak the strong.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: The softest thing in the world dashes against and overcomes the hardest; that which has no substantial existence enters where there is no crevice.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: Therefore the sufficiency of contentment is an enduring and unchanging sufficiency.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: Constant action overcomes cold; being still overcomes heat. Purity and stillness give the correct law to all under heaven.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: The tree which fills the arms grew from the tiniest sprout; the tower of nine storeys rose from a small heap of earth; the journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: Man at his birth is supple and weak; at his death, firm and strong. Thus it is that firmness and strength are the concomitants of death; softness and weakness, the concomitants of life.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: Every one in the world knows that the soft overcomes the hard, and the weak the strong, but no one is able to carry it out in practice.
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.text: The superior man is satisfied and composed; the mean man is always full of distress.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: The wise find pleasure in water; the virtuous find pleasure in hills. The wise are active; the virtuous are tranquil.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Good people walk on whatever befall, the good do not prattle, longing for pleasure; whether touched by happiness or sorrow wise people never appear elated or depressed.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: He who has given up both victory and defeat, he, the contented, is happy.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: He who has tasted the sweetness of solitude and tranquillity, is free from fear and free from sin, while he tastes the sweetness of drinking in the law.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: 'All created things perish,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way to purity.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Give up what is before, give up what is behind, give up what is in the middle, when thou goest to the other shore of existence; if thy mind is altogether free, thou wilt not again enter into birth and decay.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Thou hast made me endless, such is thy pleasure. This frail vessel thou emptiest again and again, and fillest it ever with fresh life.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Now it is time to sit quite, face to face with thee, and to sing dedication of life in this silent and overflowing leisure.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Leave all thy burdens on his hands who can bear all, and never look behind in regret.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: If thou speakest not I will fill my heart with thy silence and endure it. I will keep still and wait like the night with starry vigil and its head bent low with patience.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: In the night of weariness let me give myself up to sleep without struggle, resting my trust upon thee.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Give me the strength lightly to bear my joys and sorrows.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: When tumultuous work raises its din on all sides shutting me out from beyond, come to me, my lord of silence, with thy peace and rest.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Deliverance is not for me in renunciation. I feel the embrace of freedom in a thousand bonds of delight.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: On many an idle day have I grieved over lost time. But it is never lost, my lord. Thou hast taken every moment of my life in thine own hands.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Days and nights pass and ages bloom and fade like flowers. Thou knowest how to wait.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Even so, in death the same unknown will appear as ever known to me. And because I love this life, I know I shall love death as well.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: When I give up the helm I know that the time has come for thee to take it. What there is to do will be instantly done. Vain is this struggle.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; For love is sufficient unto love.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: But let there be spaces in your togetherness, And let the winds of the heavens dance between you.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: You may give them your love but not your thoughts, For they have their own thoughts.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: It is when you give of yourself that you truly give.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Your joy is your sorrow unmasked. And the selfsame well from which your laughter rises was oftentimes filled with your tears.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: And if it is a fear you would dispel, the seat of that fear is in your heart and not in the hand of the feared.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Say not, "I have found the truth," but rather, "I have found a truth."
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: In the bosom of such as these the spirit dwells in rhythmic silence.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Yet the timeless in you is aware of life's timelessness, And knows that yesterday is but today's memory and tomorrow is today's dream.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: For life and death are one, even as the river and the sea are one.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Every moment think steadily as a Roman and a man to do what thou hast in hand with perfect and simple dignity, and feeling of affection, and freedom, and justice, and to give thyself relief from all other thoughts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: For a man cannot lose either the past or the future: for what a man has not, how can any one take this from him?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: For nowhere either with more quiet or more freedom from trouble does a man retire than into his own soul, particularly when he has within him such thoughts that by looking into them he is immediately in perfect tranquillity; and I affirm that tranquillity is nothing else than the good ordering of the mind.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, "I have been harmed." Take away the complaint, "I have been harmed," and the harm is taken away.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Time is like a river made up of the events which happen, and a violent stream; for as soon as a thing has been seen, it is carried away, and another comes in its place, and this will be carried away too.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break, but it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: How easy it is to repel and to wipe away every impression which is troublesome or unsuitable, and immediately to be in all tranquillity.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: When thou hast been compelled by circumstances to be disturbed in a manner, quickly return to thyself, and do not continue out of tune longer than the compulsion lasts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is in our power to have no opinion about a thing, and not to be disturbed in our soul; for things themselves have no natural power to form our judgments.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Confine thyself to the present.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If you love an earthen vessel, say it is an earthen vessel which you love; for when it has been broken you will not be disturbed.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil flow of life.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Disease is an impediment to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Never say about anything, I have lost it, but say I have restored it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Remember that in life you ought to behave as at a banquet.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Remember that it is not he who reviles you or strikes you, who insults you, but it is your opinion about these things as being insulting.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if you once gain time and delay, you will more easily master yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Everything has two handles, the one by which it may be borne, the other by which it may not.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: In every station of life you will find amusements, relaxations, and enjoyments; that is, provided you be willing to make light of evils rather than to hate them.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Know then that every station of life is transitory, and that what has ever happened to anybody may happen to you also.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Solitude will cure us when we are sick of crowds, and crowds will cure us when we are sick of solitude.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Men's minds ought to have relaxation: they rise up better and more vigorous after rest.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Thus it is: we do not receive a short life, but we make it a short one, and we are not poor in days, but wasteful of them.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: He who disposes of all his time for his own purposes, who arranges all his days as though he were arranging the plan of his life, neither wishes for nor fears the morrow.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text:
I exist as I am, that is enough,
If no other in the world be aware I sit content,
And if each and all be aware I sit content.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text:
I am larger, better than I thought,
I did not know I held so much goodness.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text:
Do I contradict myself?
Very well then I contradict myself,
(I am large, I contain multitudes.)
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text:
Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road,
Healthy, free, the world before me,
The long brown path before me leading wherever I choose.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text:
I celebrate myself, and sing myself,
And what I assume you shall assume,
For every atom belonging to me as good belongs to you.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself. Nothing can bring you peace but the triumph of principles.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds, adored by little statesmen and philosophers and divines.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: It is easy in the world to live after the world's opinion; it is easy in solitude to live after our own; but the great man is he who in the midst of the crowd keeps with perfect sweetness the independence of solitude.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: For everything you have missed, you have gained something else; and for everything you gain, you lose something.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Insist on yourself; never imitate.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
And sings the tune without the words,
And never stops at all.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text:
If I can stop one heart from breaking,
I shall not live in vain;
If I can ease one life the aching,
Or cool one pain,
Or help one fainting robin
Unto his nest again,
I shall not live in vain.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text:
The soul selects her own society,
Then shuts the door;
On her divine majority
Obtrude no more.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: I learned this, at least, by my experiment; that if one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer. Let him step to the music which he hears, however measured or far away.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Give up the feeling of responsibility, let go your hold, resign the care of your destiny to higher powers, be genuinely indifferent as to what becomes of it all, and you will find not only that you gain a perfect inward relief, but often also, in addition, the particular goods you sincerely thought you were renouncing.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: Where there is sorrow there is holy ground.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.text: Another glorious Sierra day in which one seems to be dissolved and absorbed and sent pulsing onward we know not where. Life seems neither long nor short, and we take no more heed to save time or make haste than do the trees and stars.
quotes.author: John Muir
quotes.source: My First Summer in the Sierra

quotes.text: When I come back, I go to Nature to be soothed and healed, and to have my senses put in tune once more.
quotes.author: John Burroughs

quotes.text: You have seen how a man was made a slave; you shall see how a slave was made a man.
quotes.author: Frederick Douglass
quotes.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass

quotes.text: I tell you: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
quotes.author: Socrates

quotes.text: Be of good cheer about death, and know of a certainty, that no evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
quotes.author: Socrates

quotes.text: Alexander, esteeming it more kingly to govern himself than to conquer his enemies, sought no intimacy with any one of them.
quotes.author: Plutarch
